samples.question: The image is a 16x16 field of gray-noise blocks. Every block has the same mean brightness and the same variance, so no level, range, or spread cue can hide or reveal anything. But a coarse letter is encoded in the local SHAPE of the luminance distribution: a glyph-stroke block is lopsided (most pixels slightly dark, a minority quite bright, so it has a strong positive third central moment), while a background block is symmetric gray noise (zero skewness). Compute the local luminance SKEWNESS of every block so the lopsided stroke blocks light up and the letter appears. Which letter is revealed, T or L? Answer T or L.
